text:
SASRec predicts the next item at each position using a causally masked history ([original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781)). For the hybrid diagnostic, carry each sequence prefix alongside its hidden feature: position t uses h_t and sequence[:t+1] to score both positive[t] and negative[t] through the actual hybrid scorer. Never reuse the complete sequence or final-position graph context for earlier positions. Mask padding and invalid targets; run in evaluation mode without gradients. Report positive/negative scores, their margin, pairwise accuracy, and valid-pair counts, with explicit definitions. Hidden-feature dot products alone omit the transition component.

A causal Transformer mask does not prevent contamination through graph statistics. If the diagnosed user's target interaction contributed to transition counts, the graph can directly strengthen the positive candidate. Such margins measure in-sample fit and potentially memorization, rather than establish next-item generalization. Research on target-link inclusion documents related overfitting, distribution-shift, and leakage problems ([primary study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00899)). Training-target inclusion is distinct from leaking held-out validation interactions; the latter must remain excluded entirely.

Recommended diagnostic adaptation: report ordinary training-graph scores beside leave-one-user-out graph scores. For user u, subtract all of u's training contributions, then recompute affected counts, normalization, popularity terms, and derived graph features; preserve the same prefixes, candidates, and trained Transformer. Removing one edge occurrence is insufficient when repeated interactions or other user-derived associations remain. Label this graph-only exclusion: model parameters still learned from u, so it is not full leave-one-user-out evaluation. A large margin drop suggests dependence on self-contributed associations. Use the pinned macro validation HR@10 to establish generalization.
